title: candidate-feedback-draft-linda-garcia-2026-04-20
content:
Quick notes after loop with Linda Garcia (frontend engineer candidate) - rough scratchpad for debrief. Meeting length: ~60m. Interviewers: Priya (UI infra), Jordan (performance), Ethan (systems + culture).

High-level impression:
- Smart, good product sense, pragmatic engineer. Clear tradeoff thinking when asked about latency vs cost.
- Strong JavaScript fundamentals, React experience (3.5+ years), some experience with performance optimization on complex apps.
- Limited exposure to low-level infra (WebSockets, long-polling) and GPU-backed features we use for streaming - but willing to learn.

Strengths:
- Problem decomposition: broke down a streaming UI buffering problem into UX + infra layers nicely. Proposed caching + optimistic rendering approach that was reasonable.
- Ownership examples: led a cross-team initiative to migrate a legacy dashboard to a component library; described tradeoffs and stakeholder coordination well.
- Communication: concise, wrote out edge cases during whiteboard, asked clarifying Qs.

Areas of concern / gaps:
- No production experience with high-throughput websocket fanouts or managing tokenized streaming at scale. Hasn't worked directly with GPU-based inference frontends.
- Some gaps in typed-systems: primarily used JS/React; limited TS/strict typing in older codebases. Could be ramped but will take time.
- Only light backend familiarity (node microservices, but not heavy systems design).

Coding exercise (live pair):
- Solved core problem (debounced batch update + rollback) but missed a race condition initially - corrected after hint. Implementation was readable; would need tests. Time management was fine.

Culture match / signals:
- Emphasized ship-first mentality and close partnership with product/DS - aligns with PLG/dev-first culture. Values mentoring and code review.
- Expressed interest in observability and improving latency metrics templates - could be good fit for console/observability cross-collab.

Recommendation (prelim):
- Yes, with caveats. Recommend hiring at level IC3 (mid-level senior frontend) OR IC4 if we have strong banding need but only if paired with senior SWE who can cover infra/system gaps. Would add as strong product-engineer contributor; ramp plan to include shadowing on streaming infra, pair with an infra mentor for 3 months.

Suggested interview follow-ups / homework:
- Small take-home focused on building a minimal streaming UI that consumes a chunked API and handles order/race conditions + tests (2-3 hours). This will validate ownership on streaming behavior and typed code.
- Optional: short convo with SRE/serving-runtime engineer to surface infra concepts (15-30m).

Open questions to resolve in debrief:
- Compensation band expectation (candidate gave a range verbally; need confirm via recruiter).
- Remote policy - candidate prefers hybrid; confirm availability for odd hours overlap with west-coast.
- Confirm familiarity with TypeScript tooling (linting, strict mode) - resume says TS but interview leaned JS.

Next steps:
- Share notes in hiring channel, request take-home from candidate if team wants deeper validation. Priya to ping recruiter for comp / logistics. Jordan to run short infra call if we move forward.

Notes to self: mark "race condition" example in feedback form as "needed prompting" (affects coding rubric). Add link to candidate GH repo if provided later.

-- Ethan
